Question: What is your review of the Avengers 4: Endgame teaser trailer (December 2018)?
Old_Answer: The traile… oops! The teaser gave a glimpse (a really short one) of the movie, but with hidden messages, which most comic fanatics might have noticed. Endgame references from Avengers: Infinity war And Avengers: Age of Ultron This brief moment in Age of Ultron isn’t just important to Endgame simply because it drops the title. It’s important because the moment as a whole is there to remind the Avengers why they’re there. Not just to protect the people of Earth from themselves, but to protect them from even greater threats, that Tony has seen up-close and personal, that could destroy their entire world. Tony lost in space This much-anticipated trailer starts with a shot of Iron Man's helmet, badly broken in the wake of his last fight with Thanos. He's seemingly all alone on a spaceship, without power, floating along. He's recording a message to Pepper Potts on his helmet, adding in a little humor. This could be immediately following the end of Infinity War, which would imply that Nebula (Karen Gillan) is potentially on the same ship. This is Nebula’s hand which, I assume, is touching Tony's shoulder. Thanos scarecrow Thanos is briefly shown tilling the fields on his quiet farm, basking in the glory of having just murdered half of all life in the universe. And as he does so, the trailer features a shot of his old armor, now propped up as a bizarre sort of scarecrow. This scene draws inspiration directly from the 1991's comics Infinity Gauntlet Thanos is actually shown retiring from villainy and tilling the fields on a remote alien world. In that story, Thanos is retreating in disgrace more than gloating over a hard-won victory. As in the movie, Thanos acquires the full Infinity Gauntlet in this story and uses it to wipe out half of all life in the universe. The difference is that he quickly loses the Gauntlet due to his own hubris and has his work quickly undone. Thanos realizes that deep down, he always wanted to lose. Faced with his own psychological weakness, Thanos retires to live a quiet, simple life. He even uses his costume as a scarecrow just as he does in this movie. Ronin Jeremy Renner suited up in black and gold, weilding a weird katana-esque blade on the streets of a rainy Japanese city. Ronin was an identity that Clint Barton used, instead of Hawkeye, from about 2007 to 2010 in Marvel Comics. Why the name, costume and weapons change? Well, in 2004, Clint died. Then, in 2007, he was brought back to life. While he was dead, the world had necessarily moved on. A young avenger named Kate Bishop was calling herself Hawkeye — and wearing a purple costume and using trick arrows — and Clint thought she was doing pretty well with the name. Wishing additionally to hide his return from the wider world for a bit, he borrowed a code name, costume and weapons from a fallen Avenger, Maya Lopez, to become Ronin. In Avengers: Endgame, he may have darker motivations. For all we knew, in Infinity War, Clint Barton had retired from the superhero game. A tie in comic and the movie itself confirmed that he’d taken a plea deal after breaking the Sokovia Accords in Captain America: Civil War, and returned home to his family's farm. What could have dragged him away from his wife and kids? “We lost, all of us,” Captain America says in the Endgame trailer. But he says “we lost family” just as the trailer cuts to Clint in Japan, moodily wiping his blade on one arm. Did Clint Barton’s family survive the snap? Odds are not looking so good. Scott Lang Avengers: Endgame’s trailer sets up a surprising reveal: the surviving Avengers presumed that Scott Lang, aka Ant-Man, was killed when Thanos wiped out half of the universe’s life, only to have him turn up on their doorstep at the end of the trailer. A post-credits scene from Ant-Man and the Wasp explains that while other people on Earth were shattering into dust following Thanos’ snap, Ant-Man was in the quantum realm. Ant-Man may not have been killed by Thanos’ snap — officially referred to as the Decimation, according to Marvel Comics — possibly because he wasn’t within the universe at the time. While Lang is exploring the quantum realm, he’s warned to look out for time vortexes, whose name implies that if he passes through, could reconfigure time itself. This means when Lang teams up with the Avengers — or the remaining Avengers — they could use those time vortexes to reverse time and save the population from devastation. How Scott gets out of the quantum realm is a mystery. Now, the issue with Avengers trailers — or any movie trailer — is you can’t trust them. Remember that the Hulk starred in Avengers: Infinity War’s trailers and then never appeared in the actual film. This could just be a cool gesture to throw fans from guessing what’s going to happen — like we are — but this does help to explain how the Avengers could possibly defeat Thanos going forward. Did I love the trailer? Absolutely!!!
